headline: Denver Opens First Housing for Homeless College Students
meta_description: Denver's first student residence for homeless college students opens near the Capitol building, offering safe housing and support to help students earn degrees.
summary_short: A new housing program in Denver helps homeless college students find stable shelter and complete their degrees, with a proven track record of success.
body:
Denver has opened its first student residence specifically designed for homeless college students, marking an expansion of a national program that has already helped hundreds of students across four major cities. The residence, housed in a restored 1890s brick building near the Capitol building, can shelter up to 15 students and is expected to serve about 110 students annually in partnership with Metropolitan State University of Denver and Regis University. The Dax Program, created by nonprofit DePaul USA in 2015, provides more than just a roof: students receive food pantries, financial literacy workshops, employment assistance, and community support like Sunday dinners and movie nights. Residents must work at least 10 hours weekly, maintain good academic standing, and pay reduced-cost rent—a structure designed to foster independence rather than dependency.

The program addresses a crisis that extends far beyond Denver. A recent nationwide survey found that roughly half of college students experience housing insecurity, with about 14 percent homeless. Many live out of their cars or avoid community shelters, making campus-based housing critical. At MSU Denver, staff help 80 to 90 homeless students annually, while Regis aids four to six per year. Nikya Harrell, who moved into the new Denver residence after struggling through winters at Chicago's Malcolm X College—surviving on one meal per week and bouncing between family members' homes—embodies the program's impact. With her own space for the first time, she gained stability to pursue poetry, join student government, and plan for graduation from DePaul University in 2029 with a degree in early childhood education. Nationally, about 95 percent of Dax residents find permanent housing after the program, and 84 percent remain in school or graduate. "You're never alone," Harrell tells other students facing housing challenges—a message the Denver residence now makes concrete.
quick_facts: Denver residence houses up to 15 students in restored 1890s Capitol Hill building
About 95% of program participants find permanent housing afterward
Nationwide survey: roughly 50% of college students experience housing insecurity
Program operates in Chicago, Los Angeles, Philadelphia, and New York since 2015
Residents work 10+ hours weekly, pay reduced rent, maintain academic standing
